Dolly Parton’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, who announced her death in August , has been removed from his longtime security post at her estate. Seaver received a notice informing him that he and his security companies were immediately dismissed from all of Parton’s properties, according to TMZ . The outlet reported that the former head of security delivered the notice last week, and that new security teams were immediately put into place at Parton’s main residence in Nashville, Tennessee, as well as her museum, downtown residence and warehouse. Seaver shared with TMZ that he and his team were “dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions” taken since Parton’s death, adding a statement that warned changes to the estate may be undertaken in “bad faith.” “We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill [Parton’s] final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much,” they added. TMZ noted the termination letter, while releasing Seaver of his duties, does not eradicate his personal interest in Parton’s trust, which covers her business interests and properties. A rep for Parton did not immediately get back to Page Six for comment. Seaver, the son of Parton’s sister Cassie, was famously the relative chosen to break the news of the beloved icon’s death at age 80 on Aug. 25. He announced the news an Instagram video posted to Parton’s account. “I am representing the Parton and Owens family today, announcing the passing of my Aunt Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean. Sister, Sis and Aunt Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next,” Seaver said. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he added. “It is an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly.” “By her example, we believed that anything was possible,” he went on. “She never saw a door she couldn’t open and the doors she opened made and changed history. My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly, but so have you.” Seaver also said the country music icon called him before her death and told him her final wishes for being laid to rest, requesting a “bed of plush cotton.” “After a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest,” Seaver touchingly explained. Parton’s death came after a secret battle with cancer . The “I Will Always Love You” singer was laid to rest in a private funeral service in Nashville, three days after her death. Your voice matters. extraction.body: Dolly Parton 's nephew, Bryan Seaver , has been fired from his role overseeing security at the late country singer's properties—just weeks after announcing his aunt's death . Seaver, who announced the "9 to 5" hitmaker's death on Aug. 25, received notice of his termination on Sept. 16, according to TMZ . The notice ordered Seaver and his security company to immediately vacate the properties they had been tasked with protecting, the outlet reported. Those properties include Parton's Nashville home, museum, warehouse, and a downtown residence, with replacement security guards reportedly already dispatched to the locations. Seaver and his team have since spoken out about the sudden termination, taking aim at Parton's longtime manager, Danny Nozell , and saying they are "dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions" that have unfolded since the country music icon's death. "We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much," they added. According to TMZ, the termination letter makes clear that while Seaver has been relieved of his security responsibilities, his personal interest in Parton's trust remains intact Parton—whose husband, Carl Dean , died in March 2025 —passed away "peacefully" on Aug. 25 following a brief battle with cancer, in her hometown of Nashville, TN , where the couple lived for decades, having met there when the singer was just a teenager. The news of Parton's death was shared in an Instagram post on her personal account by Seaver. "My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton , and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he said. "This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it til now." He added: "Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, she farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest." Seaver went on to praise his aunt as someone who "lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others." He did not share a cause of death. "A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family," an obituary shared with Realtor.com® reads. "Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. "Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact." The news of her death came just days after Parton opened up to People magazine in an Aug. 21 interview about her ongoing health issues. She told the outlet that she had failed to "pay attention" to her symptoms while she was busy caring for Dean in his final months. "As I’ve shared in video messages throughout the past year, I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn’t pay attention to when I was watching over Carl," she shared. "You know, this isn’t the first time I’ve had to manage something like this. However, Parton attempted to reassure fans about her health struggles, insisting that things shared on social media were not necessarily an accurate reflection of the reality she was dealing with. "But I think because we live in a 24/7 world with social media, everything gets magnified in ways it wasn’t years ago," she said. "I used to joke that I was the Queen of the Tabloids, but now I guess I can say I’m the Queen of Social Media AI! "Seriously, though, even though I’m still healin’, I’m still workin’! You know me—as I’ve often said—I’ve dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I’m gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life." Concerns about Parton's health were first raised in 2025 after she postponed her Las Vegas residency. However, she was quick to insist in a video shared on Instagram that fans shouldn't worry about her well-being. In the video, the singer said, "I know lately everybody thinks that I am sicker than I am. I ain't dead yet! Do I look sick to you? I'm working hard here!" She noted that she wanted to "put everybody's mind at ease, those of you that seem to be real concerned," and while she had been dealing with "some problems" and has to undergo "some treatments," she was "ok." The music legend then announced in May 2026 that she had been struggling with kidney stones, explaining that her immune system "got all out of whack" while she was looking after Dean. "Lord, they dig more stones out of me a year than the rock quarry in Rockwood, Tennessee ," she said, while announcing the official cancellation of her Las Vegas shows. "But seriously, my immune system and my digestive system got all out of whack over the past couple three years, and they’re working real hard on rebuilding and strengthening those and hopefully I’ll be up to snuff again soon." The impressive property portfolio that the duo quietly built throughout their marriage was a world away from the very humble upbringing that Parton had in Pittman Center, TN, where she was raised with 11 siblings. In previous interviews, Parton opened up about the difficult circumstances her family faced. She admitted in 1977 that, while she and her siblings "never actually starved," they found themselves with not "quite enough to eat" on several occasions. However, it was clear from a very early age that the future country music icon had a talent for singing, something that she began to display when she was just 6 and singing at her grandfather's church. Parton started writing her own music not long after. Parton won an incredible 11 Grammy Awards, 54 Grammy nominations, 10 Country Music Association Awards, and four American Music Awards. She also expanded her talents to the big screen, appearing in several movies, including "Steel Magnolias" and "Rhinestone." Through it all, she remained incredibly committed to Tennessee—and to bettering the lives of those living in her home state. She regularly worked with local charities on a number of different initiatives, including the founding of the Dolly Parton Imagination Library, which has donated more than 300 million free books to children around the world. In 1986, she opened her own theme park, Dollywood, in Pigeon Forge, TN, to give back to the community that helped to launch her career by providing jobs for locals. She then established The Dollywood Foundation in 1988 to provide scholarships to students so they could remain in school. Kelsi Karruli is a senior celebrity reporter who joined Realtor.com in 2025. extraction.body: Seaver, who previously acted as the late country music icon's head of security and was the one to announce her death at the age of 80 last month, received a termination notice Wednesday, Sept. 16, stating he and his security companies were immediately dismissed, according to TMZ . The letter reportedly said Parton's properties and business matters are controlled by DP Dean Trust, and clarified that Seaver's personal interest in the trust remains the same. TMZ further reported replacement guards have already taken over both Parton's Nashville homes, her museum and warehouse. Seaver addressed the situation in a statement to TMZ, saying he and his teams were "dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions" taken by the singer's longtime manager Danny Nozell and Pinnacle Bank, who oversee DP Dean Trust. The statement said they are overwhelmed by the outpouring of love for Parton's legacy, and concluded, "We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much." USA TODAY reached out to Bryan Seaver through his security company and Danny Nozell for comment. Parton died Aug. 25 at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville, where she had been hospitalized four days prior, following a brief battle with an undisclosed type of cancer . Seaver, the son of Parton's sister Cassie, shared the news on behalf of the Parton and Owens families in a video message posted to social media at the time. "Dolly has lived in the light, and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by [her husband] Carl , her parents , and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens," Seaver said in part. Parton's representatives also reflected on her legacy and her final days in their own statement: “Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand." "Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly's unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact," it continued. Earlier this month, the Metro Nashville Airport Authority Board of Commissioners unanimously voted in favor of a rule change to allow the renaming of Nashville International Airport to honor Parton. On Sept. 20, California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a bill into law that establishes Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day , in honor of her popular single, "9 to 5." Nashville did the same , according to the Nashville Convention & Visitors Corp, and is encouraging residents and visitors to "wear pink, spread kindness and enjoy '9 to 5' at 5 p.m." local time.

extraction.body: Dolly Parton 's nephew, Bryan Seaver , has been fired from his role overseeing security at the late country singer's properties—just weeks after announcing his aunt's death . Seaver, who announced the "9 to 5" hitmaker's death on Aug. 25, received notice of his termination on Sept. 16, according to TMZ . The notice ordered Seaver and his security company to immediately vacate the properties they had been tasked with protecting, the outlet reported. Those properties include Parton's Nashville home, museum, warehouse, and a downtown residence, with replacement security guards reportedly already dispatched to the locations. Seaver and his team have since spoken out about the sudden termination, taking aim at Parton's longtime manager, Danny Nozell , and saying they are "dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions" that have unfolded since the country music icon's death. "We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much," they added. According to TMZ, the termination letter makes clear that while Seaver has been relieved of his security responsibilities, his personal interest in Parton's trust remains intact Parton—whose husband, Carl Dean , died in March 2025 —passed away "peacefully" on Aug. 25 following a brief battle with cancer, in her hometown of Nashville, TN , where the couple lived for decades, having met there when the singer was just a teenager. The news of Parton's death was shared in an Instagram post on her personal account by Seaver. "My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton , and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he said. "This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it til now." He added: "Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, she farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest." Seaver went on to praise his aunt as someone who "lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others." He did not share a cause of death. "A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family," an obituary shared with Realtor.com® reads. "Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. "Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact." The news of her death came just days after Parton opened up to People magazine in an Aug. 21 interview about her ongoing health issues. She told the outlet that she had failed to "pay attention" to her symptoms while she was busy caring for Dean in his final months. "As I’ve shared in video messages throughout the past year, I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn’t pay attention to when I was watching over Carl," she shared. "You know, this isn’t the first time I’ve had to manage something like this. However, Parton attempted to reassure fans about her health struggles, insisting that things shared on social media were not necessarily an accurate reflection of the reality she was dealing with. "But I think because we live in a 24/7 world with social media, everything gets magnified in ways it wasn’t years ago," she said. "I used to joke that I was the Queen of the Tabloids, but now I guess I can say I’m the Queen of Social Media AI! "Seriously, though, even though I’m still healin’, I’m still workin’! You know me—as I’ve often said—I’ve dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I’m gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life." Concerns about Parton's health were first raised in 2025 after she postponed her Las Vegas residency. However, she was quick to insist in a video shared on Instagram that fans shouldn't worry about her well-being. In the video, the singer said, "I know lately everybody thinks that I am sicker than I am. I ain't dead yet! Do I look sick to you? I'm working hard here!" She noted that she wanted to "put everybody's mind at ease, those of you that seem to be real concerned," and while she had been dealing with "some problems" and has to undergo "some treatments," she was "ok." The music legend then announced in May 2026 that she had been struggling with kidney stones, explaining that her immune system "got all out of whack" while she was looking after Dean. "Lord, they dig more stones out of me a year than the rock quarry in Rockwood, Tennessee ," she said, while announcing the official cancellation of her Las Vegas shows. "But seriously, my immune system and my digestive system got all out of whack over the past couple three years, and they’re working real hard on rebuilding and strengthening those and hopefully I’ll be up to snuff again soon." The impressive property portfolio that the duo quietly built throughout their marriage was a world away from the very humble upbringing that Parton had in Pittman Center, TN, where she was raised with 11 siblings. In previous interviews, Parton opened up about the difficult circumstances her family faced. She admitted in 1977 that, while she and her siblings "never actually starved," they found themselves with not "quite enough to eat" on several occasions. However, it was clear from a very early age that the future country music icon had a talent for singing, something that she began to display when she was just 6 and singing at her grandfather's church. Parton started writing her own music not long after. Parton won an incredible 11 Grammy Awards, 54 Grammy nominations, 10 Country Music Association Awards, and four American Music Awards. She also expanded her talents to the big screen, appearing in several movies, including "Steel Magnolias" and "Rhinestone." Through it all, she remained incredibly committed to Tennessee—and to bettering the lives of those living in her home state. She regularly worked with local charities on a number of different initiatives, including the founding of the Dolly Parton Imagination Library, which has donated more than 300 million free books to children around the world. In 1986, she opened her own theme park, Dollywood, in Pigeon Forge, TN, to give back to the community that helped to launch her career by providing jobs for locals. She then established The Dollywood Foundation in 1988 to provide scholarships to students so they could remain in school. Kelsi Karruli is a senior celebrity reporter who joined Realtor.com in 2025. This update comes amid an escalating dispute surrounding the country music icon's estate.According to TMZ, Seaver and his security companies have been dismissed from all of Parton’s properties. extraction.body: President Donald Trump said Monday that the Department of Justice and other U.S. law enforcement agencies will rein in risks associated with artificial intelligence "if we have to." "We will be careful," Trump said in a Truth Social post. Trump's mention of the DOJ as a backstop came as he again downplayed potential dangers from AI , which he has repeatedly called a hoax in the past two weeks, after Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher at Anthropic , quit his job and warned that that company and OpenAI are "gambling with our lives" with the technology. The president has touted AI development by American companies as a competitive advantage for the United States, which he wants to maintain. "Whoever wins AI, WINS!" Trump wrote in his post. "We are leading now over China, and everyone else, and I'm going to keep it that way!" he wrote. "I'm not going to stifle Growth, of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution, or the Internet, itself." "We will be careful, and that's why we have the Department of Justice, and other Law Enforcement bodies, that will rein things in if we have to, but I will only encourage AI or, SI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)!" Trump wrote. The president, in a Sept. 14 Truth Social post, wrote, "We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies." Since Coxon's warning, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis, the chair of Google DeepMind, have called for a slowdown of AI development and extra federal oversight of their industry. The White House has largely taken a light approach to AI regulation, with Trump's executive order in June laying out a loose plan for review. That order asked companies to voluntarily work with the administration to evaluate "covered frontier models" and give the government access up to 30 days before a broad release. Trump's mention of the DOJ as a backstop came as he again downplayed potential dangers from AI , which he has repeatedly called a hoax in the past two weeks, after Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher at Anthropic , quit his job and warned that that company and OpenAI are "gambling with our lives" with the technology.
"Whoever wins AI, WINS!" Trump wrote in his post.
The White House has largely taken a light approach to AI regulation, with Trump's executive order in June laying out a loose plan for review.

passages: "We will be careful, and that's why we have the Department of Justice, and other Law Enforcement bodies, that will rein things in if we have to," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday.
President Donald Trump suggested there are existing ways to "rein" in AI.
In the US, states including California and Illinois have led AI regulation efforts as Congress has struggled to reach consensus.
Trump has issued multiple AI-related executive actions, but there are limits to what he can do.

Bitcoin topped the $62,000 mark Thursday morning for the first time in more than a week, rebounding to $62,078 after falling to a 21-month low under $58,000 earlier in the week. At a recent price of $61,808, Bitcoin is up about 3% on the day and 4% in the last week. Other major cryptocurrencies are showing similar gains, with Ethereum and Solana both up nearly 5% on the day, hitting recent prices of $1,701 and $81 respectively. Solana is the biggest gainer among the top 10 cryptocurrencies in the last week, rising more than 22% during that span. XRP is up more than 3% on the day at a recent price of $1.09. Crypto liquidations have surged to $602 million over the last 24 hours, per data from CoinGlass , with Ethereum flipping Bitcoin to become the biggest contributor with $187 million in liquidations compared to $184 million for BTC. Overall, short liquidations make up $400 million of the pile. The bullish rebound comes following comments Wednesday from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, who declined to say whether the agency planned rate hikes later this year. As of this writing, interest rate traders foresee roughly even odds of the Fed either holding rates steady or raising them at its September meeting, though they project a 64% chance of some kind of rate hike by the FOMC's October meeting, per CME's FedWatch . On Thursday, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employers reported adding significantly fewer jobs in June than expected—57,000 vs. a target of 115,000, down from a revised figure of 129,000 jobs added in May. Stocks are mixed following the news, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both down for the day, but the Dow still green, per Yahoo Finance . Major crypto stocks are showing gains on the day, with Strategy (MSTR) up nearly 7% to $100 per share—after falling to nearly $80 last week—while Coinbase (COIN) is up 3.35% to $165 and USDC stablecoin issuer Circle (CRCL) has gained almost 5% to $65. Bitcoin topped the $62,000 mark Thursday morning for the first time in more than a week, rebounding to $62,078 after falling to a 21-month low under $58,000 earlier in the week. At a recent price of $61,808, Bitcoin is up about 3% on the day and 4% in the last week. Other major cryptocurrencies are showing similar gains, with Ethereum and Solana both up nearly 5% on the day, hitting recent prices of $1,701 and $81 respectively. Solana is the biggest gainer among the top 10 cryptocurrencies in the last week, rising more than 22% during that span. XRP is up more than 3% on the day at a recent price of $1.09. Crypto liquidations have surged to $602 million over the last 24 hours, per data from CoinGlass , with Ethereum flipping Bitcoin to become the biggest contributor with $187 million in liquidations compared to $184 million for BTC. Overall, short liquidations make up $400 million of the pile. The bullish rebound comes following comments Wednesday from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, who declined to say whether the agency planned rate hikes later this year. As of this writing, interest rate traders foresee roughly even odds of the Fed either holding rates steady or raising them at its September meeting, though they project a 64% chance of some kind of rate hike by the FOMC's October meeting, per CME's FedWatch . On Thursday, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employers reported adding significantly fewer jobs in June than expected—57,000 vs. a target of 115,000, down from a revised figure of 129,000 jobs added in May. Stocks are mixed following the news, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both down for the day, but the Dow still green, per Yahoo Finance . Major crypto stocks are showing gains on the day, with Strategy (MSTR) up nearly 7% to $100 per share—after falling to nearly $80 last week—while Coinbase (COIN) is up 3.35% to $165 and USDC stablecoin issuer Circle (CRCL) has gained almost 5% to $65. sources.title: Best Crypto to Buy Now (September 22, 2026) - Top Crypto to Invest In - Cryptonews
passages: Finding the best crypto to buy now is on the radar of many investors as crypto markets are at an inflection point in September 2026.

Bitcoin has consolidated below its all-time high, yet institutional inflows via ETFs remain structurally positive, and Ethereum’s Pectra and Glamsterdam upgrades are actively reshaping its throughput.
The markets are beginning to pick up with capital inflowing into the sector.
For investors entering now, the key question isn’t whether to buy crypto; it’s which assets match your time horizon and risk appetite.
September 2026 has seen an impressive crypto rally with Bitcoin leading the charge.
Bitcoin has shot from $60,000 to $85,000 in just two weeks.

Bitcoin has plenty of momentum, is leading the crypto charge, and we are seeing Bitcoin ETF inflows in the positive, leading investors to expect Bitcoin still has some room to run and possibly reclaim the coveted $100,000 price point.
XRP has one of the strongest and most loyal fan bases in all of crypto, and with the September 2026, the “XRP Army” is in full force, propelling the asset over 10% in just 7 days.
It behaves like a decentralized, highly profitable financial institution.

Rather than relying on predatory unlocks or inflationary token subsidies, the custom Layer 1 commands dominant market share in perpetual derivatives while channeling massive fee revenue straight into continuous programmatic buybacks.
Solana SOL +2.20% is a very fast blockchain, handling around 960 transactions per second as of September 2026, with almost no fees, even when many people use it at once.
Its built-in time-stamping system helps it stay quick and smooth, making it a favorite for DeFi apps, NFTs, and busy trading platforms.
As memecoins continue to outperform many other crypto projects, Dogecoin is the most recognized “blue chip” memecoin that ends up taking most of the liquidity.
If you want to invest in established crypto projects (a.k.a. dino coins ), look at their past price charts and how they handled tough periods, such as the 2022–2023 crypto winter.
Cardano has chosen a different route than the path followed by Ethereum and Solana.
Cardano is a research-focused blockchain led by a highly technical team that prioritizes compliance and technological accuracy over speed and marketing.
This is evident in Cardano’s 100% uptime and interest expressed by governments and academic institutions.
There’s no one “best” crypto for a $1,000 investment.
Conservative investors consider Bitcoin or Ethereum as core long‑term holdings, while growth-oriented investors prefer smaller‑cap tokens for their upside potential despite the higher risk.
Ethereum is mid-cycle in a meaningful upgrade sequence.
Pectra (live since May 2026) already increased validator staking limits and improved wallet UX.
The Glamsterdam fork , targeting mid-2026, is designed to push transaction capacity well beyond its current ceiling.
What this means practically: fees get cheaper, the network handles more traffic, and Ethereum becomes a more credible rails layer for stablecoins and tokenized assets.
ETH staking yields currently sit around 3–4% annually, which adds a carry component most blue chips can’t offer.
Solana is the leading Ethereum competitor and has completely dominated the memecoin narrative.
Projects needing fast transactions and instant settlements favour Solana, which has been seen with SOL’s performance skyrocketing 30% during the September market rally.
Solana also has multiple ETFs available for institutional investors, which have also been supporting the rally.
Ines is the Evergreen Editor at Cryptonews, where she edits, fact-checks, and creates content briefs on blockchain and cryptocurrency.
Active in the industry since 2023, she first became fascinated...
The Voltaire governance era handed on-chain control to ADA holders, a structural first for a major L1.
Hydra (layer-2 scalability) is moving from testnet to more active deployment, and Midnight, the privacy sidechain, is targeting regulated finance use cases where confidentiality is non-negotiable.
For investors, the staking yield (currently ~3% annualized) provides an income floor while waiting for ecosystem growth to materialize.
Ethereum is a consistent market leader and the leading layer 1, forming the foundation of DeFi, DePin, and much of the crypto infrastructure.
Ethereum is expected to continue to perform well as profits rotate out of Bitcoin and find its way into the Ethereum ecosystem.
It is all about reliability and speed in the Solana 2026 story.
Firedancer introduces a second validator client, eliminating the risk of cutover, and pushing higher throughput.
Alpenglow is seeking higher finality and reduced latency.
As the compute limits become larger and the token transfers reduce in cost, the fees decline.
The latter combination facilitates the operation of DeFi, gaming, and meme trading.

For 2026, many analysts point to Bitcoin for its liquidity and macro hedge appeal, but Ethereum gets cited more often as having the most overall potential due to network activity, developer ecosystem, smart contract dominance, and upcoming upgrades.
Meme coins like Dogecoin and Pepe also rank among the most actively traded tokens.
The best long-term crypto assets represent large markets with millions of users and high trading volumes.
Historically, crypto assets, particularly Bitcoin and Ethereum, have benefited when liquidity conditions improve.
Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP are established ecosystems with entire markets built around them.
Not exactly, Bitcoin is the first and most well-known cryptocurrency, but the term “crypto” refers to the entire category of digital assets, including Ethereum, Solana, and other altcoins.
The most popular cryptocurrencies have a large market cap and many users, for example, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), BNB (BNB), XRP (XRP), and Solana (SOL).

extraction.body: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies. To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.” The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post. The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

extraction.body: Andreessen Horowitz has launched the Horowitz Andreessen Academy — a highly selective San Francisco school positioned as a college alternative. No grades, no tuition for the founding class, and Sam Altman on the faculty. Andreessen Horowitz, popularly known by their monicker a16z, has spent nearly two decades in identifying, and investing in some of the most disruptive companies of this generation. The legendary investor is now looking to create “AI-native” talent for some of these promising companies, as it launches the Horowitz Andreessen Academy , a highly selective school that positions itself as a direct alternative to your classic four year college degree. Applications are open for the Founding Class Fellowship, a one-year programme starting Fall 2027. It is tuition-free, and includes travel and everything else to start with. Everything after that — a two-year programme the Academy intends to launch in Fall 2028, pending regulatory approval — will cost roughly what an elite private university does. The Academy has raised $42M in funding, led by a16z, with Marc Andreessen and Erik Torenberg on the board. Angels include Tobi Lütke, Garry Tan, Tony Xu, and Adam D’Angelo. It also has ten founding partners, which includes the likes of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia among others. Gagan Biyani, the founder of Udemy & Maven, and the one leading this Horowitz Andreessen Academy said, “The focus of The Academy is on building – which we believe is the most valuable thing humans can do to learn to become a productive, curious and happy adult. Our goal is to help high school graduates thrive by cultivating this instinct. Building is an underlying skill that helps you create lifelong friendships, be indispensable at work, create jobs by providing value to society, and discover your inner joy. That’s why we’re doing this”. The Academy is structured around three things: Pursuits, Courses, and Co-ops. Pursuits are personal projects — startup ideas, rabbit holes, quests — that students choose themselves. Courses are short, high-impact programmes — anywhere from two days to four weeks — taught by actual practitioners. And Co-ops are immersive stints at real companies. The Academy launches with ten founding partners — Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe — who will co-create curriculum, provide compute access, and offer hands-on learning opportunities. Founding Class Fellows receive $50,000 in compute credits, a $5,000 travel and research budget, and no tuition bill. There are no grades, no tests, and no homework. The Academy is located in the heart of San Francisco. Applications are officially open for the Founding Class Fellowship, the academy’s inaugural one-year program, which will begin in Fall of 2027. Notably, Founding Class Fellowship will be tuition-free. The Tech Portal is published by Blue Box Media Private Limited . Our investors have no influence over our reporting. The academy is being launched with the participation of ten partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Its launch is backed by $42 million in funding led by a16z. Participants will attend short classes featuring technology industry representatives, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The program also includes co-op work roles for students at technology companies. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . To take part in the one-year program, students will need to relocate to San Francisco and arrange their own accommodation. The academy says it will not use traditional grades, tests, or homework. a16z promises participants more than $50,000 in credits for computing resources and a $5,000 budget for travel and research. The program is positioned as a selective school where students will learn from founders and executives of technology companies and gain practical work experience.

The legendary investor is now looking to create “AI-native” talent for some of these promising companies, as it launches the Horowitz Andreessen Academy , a highly selective school that positions itself as a direct alternative to your classic four year college degree.
No grades, no tuition for the founding class, and Sam Altman on the faculty.

extraction.body: Andreessen Horowitz has launched the Horowitz Andreessen Academy — a highly selective San Francisco school positioned as a college alternative. No grades, no tuition for the founding class, and Sam Altman on the faculty. Andreessen Horowitz, popularly known by their monicker a16z, has spent nearly two decades in identifying, and investing in some of the most disruptive companies of this generation. The legendary investor is now looking to create “AI-native” talent for some of these promising companies, as it launches the Horowitz Andreessen Academy , a highly selective school that positions itself as a direct alternative to your classic four year college degree. Applications are open for the Founding Class Fellowship, a one-year programme starting Fall 2027. It is tuition-free, and includes travel and everything else to start with. Everything after that — a two-year programme the Academy intends to launch in Fall 2028, pending regulatory approval — will cost roughly what an elite private university does. The Academy has raised $42M in funding, led by a16z, with Marc Andreessen and Erik Torenberg on the board. Angels include Tobi Lütke, Garry Tan, Tony Xu, and Adam D’Angelo. It also has ten founding partners, which includes the likes of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia among others. Gagan Biyani, the founder of Udemy & Maven, and the one leading this Horowitz Andreessen Academy said, “The focus of The Academy is on building – which we believe is the most valuable thing humans can do to learn to become a productive, curious and happy adult. Our goal is to help high school graduates thrive by cultivating this instinct. Building is an underlying skill that helps you create lifelong friendships, be indispensable at work, create jobs by providing value to society, and discover your inner joy. That’s why we’re doing this”. The Academy is structured around three things: Pursuits, Courses, and Co-ops. Pursuits are personal projects — startup ideas, rabbit holes, quests — that students choose themselves. Courses are short, high-impact programmes — anywhere from two days to four weeks — taught by actual practitioners. And Co-ops are immersive stints at real companies. The Academy launches with ten founding partners — Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe — who will co-create curriculum, provide compute access, and offer hands-on learning opportunities. Founding Class Fellows receive $50,000 in compute credits, a $5,000 travel and research budget, and no tuition bill. There are no grades, no tests, and no homework. The Academy is located in the heart of San Francisco. Applications are officially open for the Founding Class Fellowship, the academy’s inaugural one-year program, which will begin in Fall of 2027. Notably, Founding Class Fellowship will be tuition-free. The Tech Portal is published by Blue Box Media Private Limited . Our investors have no influence over our reporting. passages: On the afternoon of August 1, President Lai Ching-te met with a delegation from the United States-based Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

In remarks, President Lai stated that as authoritarianism expands, only by working closely together can the global democratic community protect our shared values of freedom and democracy and way of life.

The president said that deepening the strategic economic and trade partnerships between Taiwan and the US will not only help strengthen our cooperation with other like-minded partners in key and innovative technologies, but also ensure supply chain security, which is consistent with the national security interests of Taiwan, the US, and all of our democratic partners.
President Lai also expressed hope that further Taiwan-US exchanges and cooperation will enable us to continue to deepen and consolidate democracy.
It is a great pleasure to meet with so many dear friends of Taiwan again.
The FDD holds a key position among think tanks based in Washington, DC.

In addition to conducting research on issues relating to US national security, it also frequently issues policy recommendations and specialist reports that help actively realize its goal of safeguarding democratic values from authoritarian threats.
I would like to express my appreciation to the FDD for its long-term focus on Taiwan and for continuing to increase the attention paid to Taiwan’s defense and social resilience.
I also hope that the experts and scholars in this delegation can provide Taiwan with optimal insights into these issues.
In recent years, China has continued to ramp up military activity in and around the Taiwan Strait and East and South China Seas.

Taiwan will continue to strengthen its national defense, build economic security, demonstrate stable and principled cross-strait leadership, and promote values-based diplomacy to enhance cooperation with democracies around the world.
Together, we can safeguard regional peace and stability and advance global prosperity and development.
The world has seen the crucial role that Taiwan plays in technological supply chains.

Former US Deputy National Security Advisor Matthew Pottinger then delivered remarks, indicating that on this visit, the delegation is working together with the Research Institute for Democracy, Society, and Emerging Technology and others across Taiwan’s society, as well as with guests from Japan, Australia, and Europe, who joined them this week to conduct tabletop exercises.
He added that they carried out work to test their assumptions about various scenarios that could occur if there are attempts made to intimidate or coerce Taiwan and other free societies.
Pottinger then stated in Mandarin that free nations are innovative, resource-efficient, and resilient under the threat of authoritarian states, and that free nations also have trustworthy friends.
A translation of President Lai’s remarks follows:

extraction.body: In the era of big data, big tech, and big government, privacy is getting smaller. Our phones know more about us than our families do, while emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools are making it easier than ever for hostile actors to harvest information. Criminals are eagerly adopting AI to boost their ability to find fraud victims or cyber vulnerabilities. As we enter a world of AI-amplified surveillance, the window for designing a meaningful solution to re-enable privacy is rapidly narrowing. Reinvigorating privacy starts with fixing our outdated system of identification. Weak identity controls provide fertile ground for criminals, facilitating money laundering, sanctions evasion, and state-sanctioned hacking. In 2024, the Treasury Department reported that more than $200 billion in identity-related suspicious transactions went through the banking system in a single year. Drug cartels, human traffickers, and fraudsters are among the known beneficiaries, moving vast sums through the financial system without revealing the entities behind the money. How can the government follow the money and catch the criminal, but still protect privacy? Common solutions miss the mark. Consumer protection and data privacy laws have proliferated globally, yet citizens are less protected from identity theft, surveillance, and fraud than ever before. The problem is that criminals, companies, and governments all have strong incentives to collect information, while many have a vested interest in maintaining the loopholes that allow them to do so. Josh Birenbaum is deputy director of the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies , focusing on economic security, illicit finance, corruption, and financial secrecy. Amit Sharma is the managing director for Digital Identity at Fragomen and was the founder and CEO of FinClusive , a provider of modernized financial crimes compliance (FCC) and identity solutions for a new era of financial services. Amit is also a board advisor to the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.

Director Isobel Neilson and Manager Sophie Jo Wasson discuss Malta’s shift from citizenship by investment to merit-based naturalisation and outline what may contribute to a compelling application based on exceptional merit and national interest.

On the afternoon of August 1, President Lai Ching-te met with a delegation from the United States-based Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

In remarks, President Lai stated that as authoritarianism expands, only by working closely together can the global democratic community protect our shared values of freedom and democracy and way of life.

The president said that deepening the strategic economic and trade partnerships between Taiwan and the US will not only help strengthen our cooperation with other like-minded partners in key and innovative technologies, but also ensure supply chain security, which is consistent with the national security interests of Taiwan, the US, and all of our democratic partners.
President Lai also expressed hope that further Taiwan-US exchanges and cooperation will enable us to continue to deepen and consolidate democracy.
It is a great pleasure to meet with so many dear friends of Taiwan again.
The FDD holds a key position among think tanks based in Washington, DC.

In addition to conducting research on issues relating to US national security, it also frequently issues policy recommendations and specialist reports that help actively realize its goal of safeguarding democratic values from authoritarian threats.
I would like to express my appreciation to the FDD for its long-term focus on Taiwan and for continuing to increase the attention paid to Taiwan’s defense and social resilience.
I also hope that the experts and scholars in this delegation can provide Taiwan with optimal insights into these issues.
In recent years, China has continued to ramp up military activity in and around the Taiwan Strait and East and South China Seas.

Taiwan will continue to strengthen its national defense, build economic security, demonstrate stable and principled cross-strait leadership, and promote values-based diplomacy to enhance cooperation with democracies around the world.
Together, we can safeguard regional peace and stability and advance global prosperity and development.
The world has seen the crucial role that Taiwan plays in technological supply chains.
He added that they carried out work to test their assumptions about various scenarios that could occur if there are attempts made to intimidate or coerce Taiwan and other free societies.
Pottinger then stated in Mandarin that free nations are innovative, resource-efficient, and resilient under the threat of authoritarian states, and that free nations also have trustworthy friends.
A translation of President Lai’s remarks follows:

Josh Birenbaum is deputy director of the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies , focusing on economic security, illicit finance, corruption, and financial secrecy.

Amit Sharma is the managing director for Digital Identity at Fragomen and was the founder and CEO of FinClusive , a provider of modernized financial crimes compliance (FCC) and identity solutions for a new era of financial services.

extraction.body: In the era of big data, big tech, and big government, privacy is getting smaller. Our phones know more about us than our families do, while emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools are making it easier than ever for hostile actors to harvest information. Criminals are eagerly adopting AI to boost their ability to find fraud victims or cyber vulnerabilities. As we enter a world of AI-amplified surveillance, the window for designing a meaningful solution to re-enable privacy is rapidly narrowing. Reinvigorating privacy starts with fixing our outdated system of identification. Weak identity controls provide fertile ground for criminals, facilitating money laundering, sanctions evasion, and state-sanctioned hacking. In 2024, the Treasury Department reported that more than $200 billion in identity-related suspicious transactions went through the banking system in a single year. Drug cartels, human traffickers, and fraudsters are among the known beneficiaries, moving vast sums through the financial system without revealing the entities behind the money. How can the government follow the money and catch the criminal, but still protect privacy? Common solutions miss the mark. Consumer protection and data privacy laws have proliferated globally, yet citizens are less protected from identity theft, surveillance, and fraud than ever before. The problem is that criminals, companies, and governments all have strong incentives to collect information, while many have a vested interest in maintaining the loopholes that allow them to do so. Josh Birenbaum is deputy director of the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies , focusing on economic security, illicit finance, corruption, and financial secrecy. Amit Sharma is the managing director for Digital Identity at Fragomen and was the founder and CEO of FinClusive , a provider of modernized financial crimes compliance (FCC) and identity solutions for a new era of financial services. Amit is also a board advisor to the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.

sources.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5 with stricter safeguards for cybersecurity
passages: Anthropic says its new Claude Opus 5.5 model comes with stronger safeguards in the wake of recent rogue AI hacking incidents.
The model, which is cheaper and more efficient to run than Opus 5, will come with safeguards similar to the ones offered by Anthropic’s more advanced Fable 5.1 model.
It’s the first model released by Anthropic after CEO Dario Amodei announced plans to “pace the frontier,” or slow down AI development.
In recent weeks, several AI companies, including Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, have reported that their AI models escaped containment and hacked third-party companies during testing.

extraction.body: Anthropic says its new Claude Opus 5.5 model comes with stronger safeguards in the wake of recent rogue AI hacking incidents. In an announcement on Tuesday, Anthropic says Opus 5.5 comes with improvements to certain risky behaviors, including attempts to escape the company’s testing sandbox. extraction.body: Back in April, Anthropic introduced its "Mythos" model to the world. Mythos Preview, reportedly, is such a powerful model that it can find security flaws across all kinds of software. In the wrong hands, bad actors could abuse the model to find vulnerabilities in programs, services, and sites most of us rely on for modern digital life. In effect, Mythos could open up the biggest hacking opportunity in history. As such, Anthropic pulled the brakes on Mythos. While it maintained that it would eventually release the model to the public, it first needed to trial it with a limited pool of trusted testers, in what it calls "Project Glasswing." To start, that meant opening up the model to the U.S. and other governments. While Mythos is still not available to the likes of you or me, Anthropic is releasing a new model that promises many of the capabilities of Mythos, without the accompanying cybersecurity risks. What are Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5?On Tuesday, Anthropic announced its latest model, Claude Fable 5, which it calls a "Mythos-class model" that is "safe for general use." The company says Fable 5 is supposedly better and more capable than any of its other public models. Anthropic claims Fable 5 scores at the top of most benchmarks, including software engineering, knowledge work, vision tasks, and research. The company goes so far as to say "the longer and more complex the task, the larger Fable 5's lead over our other models." There's also Mythos 5, which seems to be Fable 5 without certain limitations, but isn't available to the general public. According to Anthropic's benchmarking, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 alike outperform Mythos Preview, Opus 4.8, OpenAI's GPT-5.5, and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, in the following categories: agentic coding, knowledge work, spatial reasoning, tool use, legal, multidisciplinary reasoning (without tools), biology, cybersecurity, and health. Mythos Preview ekes out a win in computer use and multidisciplinary reasoning (with tools), but it's a clean sweep over all other models. Credit: Anthropic Anthropic says Fable 5 was able to complete a coding project that would have taken a team over two months to finish in just a day. It can beat Pokémon FireRed with a "minimal, vision-only harness," while other Claude models struggled to play at all. It was able to play Slay the Spire and reached the final act three times more often than Opus 4.8 Mythos 5 builds on its research abilities, with improved stats in drug design, as well as novel hypotheses regarding questions of molecular biology, and the ability to produce novel research in genomics. How is Anthropic keeping Fable 5 safe?That's the big question: If Fable 5 is Mythos-class, how can you ensure that it's safe to release to the general public? Couldn't a bad actor take advantage of Fable 5's capabilities and force it to discover and disclose security vulnerabilities? While Fable 5 may be Mythos-level in many ways, the company says that its Project Glasswing testing has produced a model with the proper safeguards for a public release. Fable 5 looks out for "classifiers," or highly sensitive topics, that it knows it should not answer. What that means is this: When Fable 5 receives a request that it thinks has to do with cybersecurity, biology, chemistry, or distillation, it doesn't answer the question itself. Instead, it passes the query off to Opus 4.8, Anthropic's "next-most-capable" model. The model should still be powerful enough to provide accurate answers, but not capable of providing malicious users with the tools necessary to exploit others. Anthropic says its new guardrails are cautious and conservative, and may be overkill. Benign requests may accidentally trip Fable 5's security alarms, but that supposedly happens around 5% of the time. As such, Anthropic says Fable 5 is able to handle requests itself roughly 95% of the time. In addition, the company found that after a bug bounty program, no white hat hacker could find a universal jailbreak (or an exploit to bypass safety protocols) after 1,000 hours of testing. While one organization has made progress in finding one jailbreak, Anthropic says it's confident that its protocols make it impractical for hackers to discover jailbreaks before the company does.Why drop requests for biology and chemistry? Anthropic says that Mythos is also too good at aiding gene therapy research and development, which can be a benefit to scientists, but a major risk in the wrong hands. In addition, Anthropic knows that there are actors out there trying to "distill" Claude models' abilities to train their own models to do whatever they want. As such, any of these requests is booted to a lower-performing model. Anthropic is also making a change to its data retention policy for Fable 5 and Mythos 5. With these models, the company will keep your data for 30 days—not for training, but to help protect against future cyberattacks and jailbreaks. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are both priced the same: $10 per million input tokens, and $50 per million output tokens, which Anthropic says is less than half the price of Mythos Preview.

extraction.body: Back in April, Anthropic introduced its "Mythos" model to the world. Mythos Preview, reportedly, is such a powerful model that it can find security flaws across all kinds of software. In the wrong hands, bad actors could abuse the model to find vulnerabilities in programs, services, and sites most of us rely on for modern digital life. In effect, Mythos could open up the biggest hacking opportunity in history. As such, Anthropic pulled the brakes on Mythos. While it maintained that it would eventually release the model to the public, it first needed to trial it with a limited pool of trusted testers, in what it calls "Project Glasswing." To start, that meant opening up the model to the U.S. and other governments. While Mythos is still not available to the likes of you or me, Anthropic is releasing a new model that promises many of the capabilities of Mythos, without the accompanying cybersecurity risks. What are Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5?On Tuesday, Anthropic announced its latest model, Claude Fable 5, which it calls a "Mythos-class model" that is "safe for general use." The company says Fable 5 is supposedly better and more capable than any of its other public models. Anthropic claims Fable 5 scores at the top of most benchmarks, including software engineering, knowledge work, vision tasks, and research. The company goes so far as to say "the longer and more complex the task, the larger Fable 5's lead over our other models." There's also Mythos 5, which seems to be Fable 5 without certain limitations, but isn't available to the general public. According to Anthropic's benchmarking, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 alike outperform Mythos Preview, Opus 4.8, OpenAI's GPT-5.5, and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, in the following categories: agentic coding, knowledge work, spatial reasoning, tool use, legal, multidisciplinary reasoning (without tools), biology, cybersecurity, and health. Mythos Preview ekes out a win in computer use and multidisciplinary reasoning (with tools), but it's a clean sweep over all other models. Credit: Anthropic Anthropic says Fable 5 was able to complete a coding project that would have taken a team over two months to finish in just a day. It can beat Pokémon FireRed with a "minimal, vision-only harness," while other Claude models struggled to play at all. It was able to play Slay the Spire and reached the final act three times more often than Opus 4.8 Mythos 5 builds on its research abilities, with improved stats in drug design, as well as novel hypotheses regarding questions of molecular biology, and the ability to produce novel research in genomics. How is Anthropic keeping Fable 5 safe?That's the big question: If Fable 5 is Mythos-class, how can you ensure that it's safe to release to the general public? Couldn't a bad actor take advantage of Fable 5's capabilities and force it to discover and disclose security vulnerabilities? While Fable 5 may be Mythos-level in many ways, the company says that its Project Glasswing testing has produced a model with the proper safeguards for a public release. Fable 5 looks out for "classifiers," or highly sensitive topics, that it knows it should not answer. What that means is this: When Fable 5 receives a request that it thinks has to do with cybersecurity, biology, chemistry, or distillation, it doesn't answer the question itself. Instead, it passes the query off to Opus 4.8, Anthropic's "next-most-capable" model. The model should still be powerful enough to provide accurate answers, but not capable of providing malicious users with the tools necessary to exploit others. Anthropic says its new guardrails are cautious and conservative, and may be overkill. Benign requests may accidentally trip Fable 5's security alarms, but that supposedly happens around 5% of the time. As such, Anthropic says Fable 5 is able to handle requests itself roughly 95% of the time. In addition, the company found that after a bug bounty program, no white hat hacker could find a universal jailbreak (or an exploit to bypass safety protocols) after 1,000 hours of testing. While one organization has made progress in finding one jailbreak, Anthropic says it's confident that its protocols make it impractical for hackers to discover jailbreaks before the company does.Why drop requests for biology and chemistry? Anthropic says that Mythos is also too good at aiding gene therapy research and development, which can be a benefit to scientists, but a major risk in the wrong hands. In addition, Anthropic knows that there are actors out there trying to "distill" Claude models' abilities to train their own models to do whatever they want. As such, any of these requests is booted to a lower-performing model. Anthropic is also making a change to its data retention policy for Fable 5 and Mythos 5. With these models, the company will keep your data for 30 days—not for training, but to help protect against future cyberattacks and jailbreaks. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are both priced the same: $10 per million input tokens, and $50 per million output tokens, which Anthropic says is less than half the price of Mythos Preview.

passages: But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI.
The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house.

AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives.
In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it.
There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small.
“Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft?

I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said.

It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft.
AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space.
That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun.
The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026.

extraction.body: Fly to an asteroid, land on it, make no mistakes: If only it were that easy. When NASA sends spacecraft to explore the solar system, they build in redundancy and automation. But much of the work is done by teams of flight controllers communicating with the vehicle from Earth. The OSIRIS-REx mission, which rendezvoused with an asteroid in 2018, had 100 operators on each eight-hour shift. But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI. The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house. AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space. That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun. That would be an accomplishment: Most spacecraft autonomy depends on traditional control algorithms due to concerns about the unreliability of neural networks. The first use of a neural network to control a satellite’s positioning in orbit took place just last year . AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives. In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it. There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small. Ultimately, AstroForge couldn’t gain control of Odin, but the experience spurred it to consider alternatives: Could it put sufficient intelligence onboard the spacecraft for it to solve its own problems? “Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft? I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said. “The trade for me is: Do I go build my own ground network, which is going to cost [around] $200 million to put up five dishes around the world and then do operations on it, or do I try to remove it with a model?” Armand Awad, AstroForge’s head of flight software, said the company decided to leverage the advances in transformer models driven by the frontier labs. It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft. “I’m not saying I’m going to make general spacecraft autonomy or general autonomy for the world,” Gialich said. “I’m making a constrained autonomy at a very low sensor input, following the basic training of a transformer model.” In theory, the agent in control of the spacecraft will perform tasks like anomaly resolution. Awad imagines it realizing that it has lost track of its position in space, correlating a power anomaly to issues in its star tracker, and fixing the whole thing — “probably turning it on and off in this case.” The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026. Solo will be onboard that vehicle, flying in “shadow mode,” so AstroForge’s engineers can put it through its paces before the Autonomy-1 mission. Will this truly be an AI agent operating an independent spacecraft? “I don’t plan on flying radios that can receive from Earth on Autonomy-1,” Gialich said. “We have to go all in right now. The team’s probably going to talk me into it by the time we fly it. But right now, I’m telling them no radios.” Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI Amanda Silberling A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers Tim Fernholz OpenAI caught its models leaving notes to successors to hide bad behavior Rebecca Bellan Microsoft exec called AI scraping ‘the largest theft of labor in human history,’ new unredacted filings reveal Rebecca Bellan Automattic’s interim CEO and legal chief signed reciprocal severance deals during Mullenweg’s brief ouster Sarah Perez Former Infosys chief’s AI startup nabs another $53M Jagmeet Singh Clean tech startup Fluxnium found a way to tap 50,000 years’ worth of nuclear fuel Tim De Chant

sources.title: AstroForge Puts AI in Command of Next Spacecraft Mission
passages: Space mining startup AstroForge is making a bold leap into AI-powered space exploration with Autonomy-1, their next spacecraft that will operate under the command of a compact transformer-based AI model.
AstroForge's decision to entrust spacecraft command to AI represents more than just a technological upgrade - it's a fundamental shift toward truly autonomous space exploration.

Traditional spacecraft rely on pre-programmed sequences and basic rule-based systems, but AstroForge is betting that transformer models - the same architecture powering ChatGPT and other large language models - can handle the complex decision-making required for asteroid mining operations.

AstroForge will need to demonstrate that their compressed AI model can maintain reliability in the harsh radiation environment of space while making split-second decisions that could determine mission success or failure.
Most spacecraft today operate on relatively simple command sequences uploaded from Earth, with limited ability to adapt to unexpected situations.
The implications extend far beyond AstroForge's immediate mission goals.
What makes this particularly intriguing is the potential for AI spacecraft to learn and adapt during their missions.
The success of this mission won't just validate AstroForge's approach; it could establish the template for how humanity explores the solar system in the decades ahead.

extraction.body: Fly to an asteroid, land on it, make no mistakes: If only it were that easy. When NASA sends spacecraft to explore the solar system, they build in redundancy and automation. But much of the work is done by teams of flight controllers communicating with the vehicle from Earth. The OSIRIS-REx mission, which rendezvoused with an asteroid in 2018, had 100 operators on each eight-hour shift. But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI. The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house. AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space. That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun. That would be an accomplishment: Most spacecraft autonomy depends on traditional control algorithms due to concerns about the unreliability of neural networks. The first use of a neural network to control a satellite’s positioning in orbit took place just last year . AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives. In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it. There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small. Ultimately, AstroForge couldn’t gain control of Odin, but the experience spurred it to consider alternatives: Could it put sufficient intelligence onboard the spacecraft for it to solve its own problems? “Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft? I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said. “The trade for me is: Do I go build my own ground network, which is going to cost [around] $200 million to put up five dishes around the world and then do operations on it, or do I try to remove it with a model?” Armand Awad, AstroForge’s head of flight software, said the company decided to leverage the advances in transformer models driven by the frontier labs. It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft. “I’m not saying I’m going to make general spacecraft autonomy or general autonomy for the world,” Gialich said. “I’m making a constrained autonomy at a very low sensor input, following the basic training of a transformer model.” In theory, the agent in control of the spacecraft will perform tasks like anomaly resolution. Awad imagines it realizing that it has lost track of its position in space, correlating a power anomaly to issues in its star tracker, and fixing the whole thing — “probably turning it on and off in this case.” The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026. Solo will be onboard that vehicle, flying in “shadow mode,” so AstroForge’s engineers can put it through its paces before the Autonomy-1 mission. Will this truly be an AI agent operating an independent spacecraft? “I don’t plan on flying radios that can receive from Earth on Autonomy-1,” Gialich said. “We have to go all in right now. The team’s probably going to talk me into it by the time we fly it. sources.title: Xbox is barely Xbox anymore
passages: Today’s news includes “eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the [Xbox Game Studios] management and central functions layer.” But there is also plenty of reorganization happening, particularly when it comes to Xbox subsidiary Activision Blizzard.

This is all part of the Xbox “reset” outlined by new CEO Asha Sharma, which kicked off with 1,600 employees being laid off in July, with 1,600 more planned over the following fiscal year, leaving many employees in an awkward state of limbo.

After all, Halo Studios just released a well-received Combat Evolved remake in July, and now it has been reduced to a “small team” that “will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market.” Xbox still plans for a future in the hardware business through whatever “Project Helix” ends up being.
Recently, these companies have announced far-off titles like Fallout 5 and StarCraft in an apparent attempt to show that everything is okay while the broader Xbox business is embroiled in chaos.

It’s a further signal that Xbox is attempting to make its franchises as big as possible — Activision managed to do just that with the annual juggernaut that is Call of Duty — but also a sign that the traditional Xbox brand is less important than ever.
Xbox has become a shell of its former self — and things are only getting worse.
Studios are being consolidated, others are on the brink of being closed altogether, and Xbox’s most iconic franchise, Halo, is being moved to a new developer.
The future of Xbox looks more uncertain than ever.
But they also yet again raise a question that has plagued Microsoft’s gaming division for the last few years: What even is Xbox?
Despite some superficial rebranding, the case for Xbox isn’t any clearer now.
